questions: Do the iteration 7 metrics differ from iteration 6 (score 36.3097) on any track? If they match to four decimals, check the race data pipeline before drawing any conclusion about mass.
Does line_loss_events fall below one on the oval or s-bend, and does max_error drop below 0.06 m?
Does steering_oscillation rise sharply on the slalom with the lighter robot? If so, the limit is over-steering and the Integrator should add kd damping rather than change geometry.
Does completion or progress change on any track? Report the first step and progress at which line loss begins on each track.

intent: Test mass as the one remaining geometry lever. Hold the iteration 6 platform fixed (sensors at y = 0.07 m, ±0.03 m spread, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 × 0.18 m) and change only mass from 0.8 kg to 0.5 kg. Expect lower yaw inertia to raise yaw response per turn command, reducing max_error and line_loss_events on the oval and s-bend, with the risk of more steering oscillation on the slalom.
learning: Iterations 0 to 6 show that spread, footprint, wheel track, wheel radius and lead do not move max_error off the 0.06 m floor, and that controller gain (kp 3.0) is the only change that has improved the score so far, on the slalom. Mass is the last untested geometry lever and is the next test here. If it leaves max_error at 0.060 m or above, geometry is exhausted and the remaining levers are controller damping (kd) and base_speed.
rationale: Iteration 6 moved the score from 26.04 to 36.31. The gain is on the slalom (score 14.39 to 45.18, progress 0.035 to 0.11), while the oval and s-bend still end off track after one line-loss event with max_error at 0.061 m. Five geometry families (spread, footprint, wheel track, wheel radius, lead) left max_error at 0.060 to 0.061 m, and the 0.06 m off-track floor binds because body_width cannot lift it. The Integrator's rule (b) applies: line loss persists near 0.06 m, so the next untested geometry lever is mass. Mass has never been tested, and a lower mass lowers yaw inertia, so the robot turns faster for the same turn command. I keep the iteration 6 geometry and change only mass, from 0.8 kg to 0.5 kg, so any change against iteration 6 comes from mass. body_length is left alone because the contract says it has no dynamic effect. Expected result: max_error falls toward or below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend and line_loss_events drop, but the slalom may show more steering oscillation because the robot is more responsive. If mass does not move the metrics, geometry is exhausted and the Integrator should focus on controller damping (kd) and base_speed.
